title: U.S. House · California's 8th District
area: Covers part of the Sacramento Valley and North Bay, including Fairfield, Vallejo and Richmond, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.

In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, John Garamendi (D) placed first with 54.4% (97,155 votes) and Rudy Recile (R) placed second with 27.8% (49,599 votes) out of 178,561 total votes cast; both advanced to the general election.

candidates.name: John Garamendi
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with a majority of votes cast

summary.text: John Garamendi is the Democratic incumbent for California's 8th Congressional District, which covers much of Contra Costa and Solano counties. Before Congress he was a Peace Corps volunteer, a state legislator, California Insurance Commissioner, Deputy Secretary of the Interior and Lieutenant Governor. He serves on the House Armed Services and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

background.text: Born in Camp Blanding, Florida, according to Ballotpedia; his congressional office says he was raised in Mokelumne Hill, California.
Earned a B.A. from UC Berkeley (1966) and an M.B.A. from Harvard University (1970, per Ballotpedia).
With his wife Patti, served in the Peace Corps in Ethiopia from 1966 to 1968, teaching 7th and 8th graders; he later worked as a businessman and rancher.

Elected to the California State Legislature in 1974 and later served four terms in the state Senate; his office says he authored a state solar, wind and energy conservation tax credit and legislation that became California's assault weapons ban.
Served as California Insurance Commissioner from 1991 to 1995 and again from 2003 to 2006, and was appointed Deputy Secretary of the Interior by President Clinton in 1995.
Served as Lieutenant Governor of California from 2007 to 2009, where he chaired the State Lands Commission.

First elected to the U.S. House in a 2009 special election; now in his eighth term. Has served on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee since taking office and, in 2025-2026, on Armed Services (Readiness and Strategic Forces subcommittees).
Was chair of the Armed Services Readiness Subcommittee in 2021-2022 and its ranking member in 2023-2024.
According to his office, he lives in Northern California with his wife Patti; they have six children and 14 grandchildren.
Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

priorities.text: Past campaign materials describe support for investment in transportation, clean technology, education and research, and for extending tax savings to middle-class families and small businesses.

positions.summary: Has said every American deserves access to quality, affordable health coverage, citing his tenure as California's Insurance Commissioner.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, including its Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation, Highways and Transit, and Water Resources and Environment subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 session.
Serves on the House Committee on Armed Services, including its Readiness and Strategic Forces subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 session.

candidates.name: Rudy Recile
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary
candidates.currentRole: Retired U.S. Army Major; small business owner

summary.text: Rudy Recile is the Republican nominee for California's 8th Congressional District. A retired U.S. Army major with more than 26 years of service, he later worked for the U.S. Department of Agriculture and runs a small web business. He previously ran for the seat in 2022 and 2024.

background.text: Born in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. The Daily Republic reported in 2022 that he is a U.S. citizen of Filipino heritage and the son of a single immigrant mother who brought her family from the Philippines.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Eastern Illinois University in 1995 and a graduate degree from National Graduate School in 2005 (per Ballotpedia).
Served in the U.S. Army from 1988 to 2014, with assignments in Illinois, South Korea and Washington, D.C., including time at the Pentagon; his final duty station was in Fairfield, California.
The Daily Republic reported he worked as a logistician and project manager, and as a contract officer representative for the Army.
After retiring in 2014 he settled in California, worked as a USDA data manager and instructor in its Plant Protection and Quarantine division, and owns a web development business.

Has been affiliated with Veterans of Foreign Wars Post 2333 (Fairfield-Suisun), the National Rifle Association, the California Rifle and Pistol Association, and the Solano and Yolo County Republican central committees.
Ran for this seat in 2022 and 2024 and lost to Garamendi both times; in the June 2026 primary he finished second with 27.8%.
Links to a podcast, "Boot's on the Ground," according to his campaign website.

priorities.text: Lists platform issues including energy independence, support for the Bill of Rights, government spending accountability, public safety, support for veterans, California water issues, and education.
priorities.quote: My platform issues include energy independence, supporting the Bill of Rights, tax dollars accountability, public safety, supporting veterans, California's water issues and quality education.

researchNotes: Neither candidate has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. Garamendi's priorities and healthcare position are drawn from an older (2016) campaign-website excerpt reproduced on Ballotpedia, since no current 2026 issue statement was found; his committee record is current. Recile's issue positions were not detailed on his campaign homepage beyond the listed platform topics, so specific stances were not documented. Biography gaps: Garamendi's year of birth and birthplace come only from Ballotpedia (his office gives where he was raised); Recile's career dates beyond Ballotpedia and a 2022 Daily Republic profile were not found.
